title: Budget test timeout to measured reality, document why
context: MCP refusal test was flaky on Windows—fixture setup (~88-91s) pushed against 90s timeout. Core assertion proven fast (<10s), but test failed under full-suite load due to budget mismatch, not actual hang.
decision: Raised timeout from 90s to 240s and added inline comment distinguishing the fast assertion from expensive fixture spawning. Prioritizes transparency over metric gaming.
consequences: Test now passes reliably (10/10) standalone and under load
Future readers can distinguish between 'the code is slow' and 'the harness is expensive'
Sets pattern: document measured costs, don't mask them silently
Preserves evidence that the core bug (remote mismatch refusal latency) was actually fixed
alternatives_rejected: Leave at 90s and accept flakiness—ignores real measurement
Increase timeout silently—creates mystery for future maintainers
Optimize fixture setup before shipping—defers real work
Split test to reduce setup—adds complexity without proving the fixture is wrong
